methodological_rigor.justification: The study employs a multi-pronged, orthogonal approach: large-scale GPS (global protein stability) peptidomic screens on 2227 nonstop mutations plus 799 additional variants and 415 readthrough SNPs, validation via cycloheximide-chase assays and FLAG-tagged full-length constructs, CRISPR/Cas9 proteostasis sublibrary screens for E3 ligase identification, a random-peptide platform for compositional features, and cross-species bioinformatics/PCA. Biological replicates are used with high reproducibility (Fig. 1D). Limitations include HEK293T-only cell context and reliance on a fused 58-residue C-terminus rather than native full-length contexts for the screens, though full-length validation mitigates this.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is preclinical basic/molecular biology research on cell lines (HEK293T) with bioinformatic comparative analyses, mapping to Oxford LoE 5 (mechanistic/basic science). Translational relevance is plausible and articulated: the authors link stability-altering nonstop mutations to specific oncoproteins (CCND2, FOXA1, HEY1) and tumor suppressors (PTEN, MAX, CTCF), and raise concerns for readthrough-based nonsense-suppression therapies and opportunities for C-terminus-based therapeutic modulation. However, no patient data, drug development, or direct clinical application is demonstrated.

reporting_quality.justification: No animals are used, so ARRIVE is only partially applicable; the paper is best evaluated against general Nature-family/lab reporting norms with biological triplicates, defined antibody catalog numbers, sgRNA sequences in Supplementary Table 1, and a Reporting Summary linked to the Nature Portfolio. The Source Data file is explicitly provided. Methods are detailed (GPS, CRISPR, PCA, permutation tests, PSI thresholding). Minor reporting gaps include limited information on exclusion criteria in the screens and a lack of explicit blinding mention. Data availability appears strong given the Supplementary Data and Source Data files.

novelty_literature.justification: The paper directly challenges a prior systematic study (Ghosh et al.) by showing nonstop mutations can stabilize as well as destabilize proteins, re-annotating ~27% of previously neutral mutations. It introduces the finding that Cys and Trp enrichment (rather than general hydrophobicity) plus Asp/Glu depletion is the distinguishing signature of aberrant C-termini, and identifies MARCH6 and RNF139 as additional E3 ligases beyond the canonical Bag6-RNF126 pathway. It also provides a systems-level framework linking alternative splicing and programmed readthrough to protein half-life modulation. These are multiple first-in-class mechanistic contributions.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is logically organized with clearly titled results subsections that build a coherent narrative from disease mutations to splicing/readthrough to compositional rules to ligase networks. Figures are richly described in legends and integrate PCA, violin plots, bar charts, and blot panels. Some figure legends (e.g., Figs. 5-6) are dense and reference many panels; a non-specialist reader would benefit from more signposting. Mathematical notation blocks (MathJax LaTeX wrappers) appear as raw markup in the normalized text but do not impede overall comprehension.

key_strengths: Large-scale GPS peptidomic screen of >3000 nonstop/readthrough variants with robust replicate correlation and orthogonal validation in full-length constructs
Directly re-examines and overturns prior conclusions (Ghosh et al.) about the directionality of nonstop-mutation effects on protein stability
Novel identification of MARCH6 and RNF139 as E3 ligases recognizing hydrophobic C-termini beyond Bag6-RNF126, with sequence-context-dependent specificity
Cross-species PCA and random-peptide composition analysis reveal Cys/Trp enrichment plus Asp/Glu depletion as a conserved signature of aberrant C-termini
Translational framing connects findings to readthrough therapy safety and Evrysdi-Risdiplam-style splicing modulation
key_concerns: All experiments are in HEK293T cells, leaving open whether ligase specificities and PSI rankings hold in other cellular contexts or patient-relevant models
The 58-residue C-terminal fusion onto GFP is a standardized but artificial context; full-length validations are selective rather than comprehensive
Disease-relevance claims for specific oncoproteins/tumor suppressors rest on stability changes without functional tumor biology experiments
Some figure panels are information-dense; additional summary schematics would aid broader readability
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically rigorous, highly novel systems-level study that reframes a fundamental aspect of C-terminal proteostasis; the integration of large-scale screens, CRISPR, bioinformatics, and validation supports Tier 1 placement pending minor clarifications.
